name: AD847 / AD827
tagline: ADI's 50 MHz, 300 V/µs video op-amp: a 1990s CD-player and DAC upgrade favourite for dynamic sound and strong bass.

lineage.note: Sole source; SPICE model dated 12/90. AD827 is the dual of the 'industry-standard AD847'. Siblings AD848/AD849, AD817/AD826.

part_numbers.note: J grade (0 to +70 °C), DIP-8 (N-8). Pre-RoHS; probably obsolete, unconfirmed.
RoHS (Z) version of the JN; Z marks package, not die, by ADI convention.
J grade, SOIC-8 (R). Reportedly listed at Mouser.
Military grade with its own detail spec (ad847s.pdf). SQ, /883B, SMD orderables unverified.
DIP-8, J grade. JNZ stocked at Digi-Key, Arrow, Mouser (2026); JN status unknown.
16-lead plastic SO (R-16), not an SO-8 drop-in. Obsolete at Digi-Key.
S grade (military) cerdip; on a Utmel page. /883B variants unverified.

key_specs.source: AD827 data sheet; ADI textbook ch. 3

key_specs.value: ±5 V to ±15 V specified (9–36 V total)
AD847 4.8 mA, AD827 5.25 mA per amp
Bipolar NPN differential pair, voltage feedback

reputation.summary: A 1990s cult swap: video amps fitted into CD-player outputs, DAC I/V stages and headphone amps. The rec.audio FAQ called them 'the better op amps for audio'. Soomal pairs the AD847 with the AD797 for big dynamics and bass. Others hear the AD827 as warm, sweet, sharp in attack, sometimes thin in bass. No measurements found.
typical_uses: DAC I/V conversion and output filters
Video and line drivers, ADC buffers, cable driving
caveats: Bipolar input with about 3 µA bias: DC offset rises with high or unmatched source impedances.
A 50 MHz part in sockets needs tight decoupling and short leads.
About 5 mA per amp at ±5 V to ±15 V, more than NE5532-class parts.
SMD AD827 is 16-lead SO (R-16); only the DIP-8 drops into standard dual sockets.
Some find it too sweet or loose in bass; one Japanese test reported reduced gain below 200 Hz.

counterfeit_notes: No specific reports. 'Fever Dual Op Amp' marketplace listings and old non-Z JN stock are likely remark targets; buy authorized. Genuine SMD AD827 is 16-lead SO only, so SOIC-8 'AD827' is a remark. 'Replace AD827' modules aren't AD827s.

Current revision per mirror labels. Dates and changes of Rev. A to E not found.
Original model authored 'JCB / PMI' (no evidence PMI made the die): NPN input, 8.8 kHz dominant pole, unlimited-C-load output; J, A, S grades.
Re-issued (TRW/ADI header); change not described, netlist topology unchanged.

'Updated to new header style'. No electrical change stated.

refuted_claims: Product-page snippet 'consuming only 100 milliamps' is wrong: the data sheet says 100 mW from ±5 V (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD827.pdf).

AD827 SMD package confirmed as 16-lead plastic SO (R-16); row split into obsolete AD827JR-16 and AD827JRZ-16.
AD827AQ confirmed as 8-lead cerdip (Q-8); AD827SQ added.
AD847 lists a Cerdip (Q) package; ADI AD847S military spec (ad847s.pdf) added.
